analysis:
Integration pass over all ten units. The PR changes operator-facing status and doctor wording, adds an optional local diagnostic counter, and updates docs and tests. The counter is cancellationsPartialComplete in DaemonStateFile.swift (DaemonState.Stats, lines ~130-142). ProviderLoop+Trust.swift (lines 69-70) copies it from stats. StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift (new helper) is called from StatusCommand.swift line 174. DoctorRunner.swift lines 223 and 241 only reword messages.

Security-relevant observations:
- The new field is an optional UInt64 aggregate. It carries no prompt content (A-001), keys (A-003), tokens (A-008), attestation or authorization evidence (A-015, A-016).
- The optional field keeps older state files decodable.
- No changes touch the coordinator WebSocket wire contract (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011, T-052 to T-054), the encrypted prefix-cache tier (T-041, SEC-035), the fan helper (TB-010) or key handling.
- The state-file counters remain self-reported diagnostic data. The text says they are not paid-job records and points to the console Earnings page. It makes no payment-authority, secrecy or correct-computation claims (T-056).
- The tests (unit 9) use temp directories and a loopback placeholder URL. They introduce no secrets or network I/O.

Unverified, none a demonstrated regression:
- Where stats.cancellationsPartialComplete is defined and incremented in the ProviderLoop stats struct is not in the supplied evidence.
- The platform heartbeat.go cumulativeDelta semantics are platform-owned.
- The owner-only permissions of daemon-state.json are pre-existing and unchanged here.
- The integration source replay was incomplete (43 units omitted). I examined the supplied changed files and found no issue.
